### LOW: Dev release channel shares bundle ID and signing identity with production, but the threat model has no coverage
[\.github/workflows/release\-swift\.yml:15](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aa4c38498ecce14a9039d9602e59fa991d0fc563/.github/workflows/release-swift.yml#L15) · T-053, T-054, T-055

The new comment states that a dev release is packaged with a different app name and executable name, while the bundle identifier and the Developer ID signing identity stay the same as production\. The dev app is meant to install beside the production app\. Same\-bundle\-ID builds share the Keychain access group, the App Attest app identity and, plausibly, the SE key label and provider token storage \(A\-002, A\-008, A\-015\)\. Separation then depends entirely on the coordinator qualifying the full CodeDirectory \(T\-054\)\. It also depends on credential continuity not being read as machine identity \(T\-055\)\. The threat model does not describe a dev channel, or whether a dev build may use or overwrite production credentials or tokens on the same Mac\. Fix: document the dev channel in TB\-011 and T\-054/T\-055, or give dev builds a distinct bundle ID, keychain group and key labels\. Also confirm that the coordinator never qualifies dev CodeDirectory hashes for production serving\.

findings.detail: The header comment states that dev releases install beside production while the bundle identifier and signing identity stay identical. The Info.plist step keeps CFBundleIdentifier=io.darkbloom.provider, and the same provisioning profile and keychain-access-group are embedded. Dev apps are published on every master push without a tag. On one Mac, a dev build can therefore load the production persistent SE key (label io.darkbloom.provider.attestation-signing.v2) and the same-app-ID App Attest credential. This lets a dev-channel binary sign attestation or challenges for the production identity. The same SE public key is also visible to both the dev and prod coordinators, which links the two environments' sessions. Existing controls such as binary-hash and CodeDirectory qualification and the per-connection process X25519 key limit the damage. Even so, this weakens the dev/prod credential separation that T-055 and T-058 assume. Fix: give the dev app a distinct bundle ID, keychain label or access group (and profile), or document and test that dev builds cannot use production credentials. Update the threat model either way.
findings.title: Dev and prod apps share one bundle ID, signing identity and keychain group, so side-by-side installs share hardware-bound credentials
